question: Does the same 58kg load impose different time cost on a small versus above-average body-mass horse?
prior_results_already_seen: Weight study v2 body-by-burden interaction was not significant after BH; new conditional contrast and pair modifier plan fixed before their estimation. Retrospective follow-up, not independent validation.
contrast: Difference between conditional time cost of 55 to 58kg at 250kg versus 300kg body mass; positive means larger cost at 250kg. Does not compare total ability or predict absolute times between two horses.
raw58: Actual carried weight exactly58, body bands under260,260to279,280to299,300plus. Counts, horses, mean/median within-race median-relative time; descriptive only. No pooled absolute time across distances.
row: Reuse full-period weight v2 race+horse FE interaction models and covariance; 3*(burden coefficient + ((body-278)/10)*burden_body coefficient). Small-minus-large difference is -15*interaction coefficient.
pair: Reuse same-ID/exact-distance/year/grade 7-60-day pairs and nuisance controls. Add mean endpoint body/10 and its square to nuisance, and unpenalized positive-change-by-body and negative-change-by-body interactions. Increase and decrease base slopes remain unpenalized. 250/300kg are mean endpoint body values, distinct from current body in row model.
pair_sensitivity: Full-period same band/month and body change <=5kg
support: Pair model >=100 pairs, >=30 horses, >=30 later dates and >20 residual df; both-example support counts body240-260 versus290-310, burden55 and58, and horses observed at both loads are explicitly shown. No unsupported inference made precise by ratios.
uncertainty: Reuse conservative date+horse clustered covariance and t df; pair earlier-endpoint date limitation persists. BH across all supported distances and both time targets for small-minus-large contrast, separately by family/period/variant.
nonclaims: Ratio alone is not a physiological penalty
No equivalence test or same-impact conclusion
No fixed ratio penalty or per-kg correction
No independent future validation or operational writes
